links.outcome: Foundation model features versus functional connectivity and dummy classifier baselines on same data
links.effect: For sex, functional connectivity outperformed all foundation model features. For MCI and β-amyloid, no feature exceeded the dummy classifier in accuracy and AUC stayed near chance.
links.quote: For MCI and β-amyloid, no feature exceeded the dummy classifier in accuracy, and the area under the curve (AUC) stayed near chance for all features.

links.outcome: Adequacy of model documentation and code for reproducing use on new data
links.effect: Both models required substantial changes to released code; BrainHarmonix documentation did not specify how to normalize new data, resolved by testing alternatives.
links.quote: BrainHarmonix’s documentation did not specify how to normalize new data, so we resolved this by testing different alternatives.

unlisted_practices: Always report simple baselines (functional connectivity and dummy classifier) when evaluating foundation models
Report multiple metrics including precision for clinical targets with strong class imbalance
Provide standardized data preprocessing workflows with released foundation models

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of two fMRI foundation models (BrainLM and BrainHarmonix) on clinical downstream prediction targets, identifying significant gaps in generalizability, usability, and baseline performance.
